update description: This sub-process describes the activities to build new or reuse existing automation-ready dissemination components needed for the release of statistical products as designated in sub-process 2.1. Dissemination modules—spanning web services, open data, geospatial outputs, microdata access, and even traditional products—are built or upgraded for modularity, machine-actionability, and AI/automation-enabled production. Dynamic output generation, versioning, metadata enrichment, and seamless integration with downstream APIs are all standard, with automation ensuring real-time release, update, and consistency of all published outputs. Human staff are responsible for policy oversight, exception handling, and refinement of complex or user-specific dissemination features that automation cannot yet address.
interdependencies: 2.1 Design outputs and dissemination - dissemination products must now be designed for modularity, automation-readiness, metadata enrichment, and API delivery, which directly shapes the officer's dissemination and custom tabulation work.

Downstream dissemination operations and support processes - automation-ready components increase dependence on monitoring, version control, exception handling, and quality assurance in release and user servicing activities.
impact reasoning: The role shifts from primarily executing and supporting dissemination tasks to overseeing and assuring automated, modular dissemination processes. Work once centered on editing, validating, marketing, and manually disseminating outputs will increasingly involve validating automated dissemination components, checking metadata and version integrity, supporting API- and open-data-based delivery, and resolving exceptions where automated release workflows fail or where user requests require non-standard handling. The position will need stronger technical fluency in automation-enabled dissemination architecture, metadata standards, interoperability, machine-actionable outputs, and release governance. The role also becomes more quality-assurance- and standards-oriented, with greater responsibility for ensuring dissemination components are compliant with confidentiality, consistency, and policy requirements across multiple channels. This also implies a future evolution toward hybrid statistical dissemination and product-operations support, where the officer contributes to refining automated release processes, user-facing dissemination features, and quality controls rather than only producing static outputs.

update description: This sub-process releases dissemination products using digital automation to handle all elements of release—timing, briefing, embargo, subscriber access, and confidential data management. update description: This sub-process provides user support through AI-powered chatbots and automation interfaces, which record, triage, and answer user queries in real time, guiding users to datasets, data interpretations, and publications as needed. Complex inquiries and escalations go to human staff for resolution, especially for nuanced, sensitive, or high-value support. User feedback and request tracking are used to populate knowledge bases and feed into service quality improvement.
interdependencies: 7.2 Disseminate products: user-support content, FAQs, and guidance become embedded in dissemination channels and product navigation
8 Quality management: user-query trends, feedback, and escalation patterns become inputs to service and product quality improvement
Knowledge base / FAQ maintenance: repeated responses are formalized into reusable support content that changes dissemination and client-service workflows
impact reasoning: The role shifts from primarily responding directly to user requests and preparing custom outputs toward a hybrid human-in-the-loop support model. Routine and repeatable inquiries will increasingly be handled by AI-enabled support tools, while the officer will focus more on escalated cases requiring judgment, contextual interpretation, confidentiality awareness, and tailored statistical guidance. The position will also contribute more systematically to maintaining support knowledge bases, improving automated responses, and interpreting user feedback for service improvement. Operationally, this changes the cadence of client interaction from mostly one-to-one service delivery to exception handling, quality assurance of automated support content, and continuous refinement of user guidance materials. This also implies stronger responsibility for identifying when automated outputs are insufficient, risky, or potentially misleading, and for translating recurring user issues into clearer dissemination materials, training content, and support procedures. Over time, the role may evolve to include stewardship of AI-assisted support workflows, monitoring escalation quality, and helping align automated support with statistical concepts, dissemination standards, and privacy obligations.
